question: Between 2012 and 2023, the EU vape market grew 4.5-fold, while nicotine pouch sales increased approximately 17-fold between 2018 and 2023. A growing range of novel nicotine products, from nicotine pouches to oral nicotine tablets, is entering our European market. In May 2026, the World Health Organization warned that manufacturers were aggressively marketing nicotine pouches to adolescents and young people.

Early nicotine exposure increases the risk of tobacco use later in life, undermining the EU’s ambition to achieve a tobacco-free generation by 2040. Meanwhile, the tobacco industry’s rapid product innovation is increasingly outpacing lawmakers’ ability to deliver timely and effective regulation. In light of the above: 1.

Does the Commission possess data on the number of nicotine products, including vapes and nicotine pouches, marketed in the EU using child-appealing flavours, packaging or branding, including products currently outside the scope of the Tobacco Products Directive1 (TPD)?

Will the Commission use this evidence in the planned revision of the TPD to establish a future-proof regulatory framework covering all nicotine-containing products, including a market freeze preventing new nicotine products and delivery devices from entering the EU market until an appropriate regulatory framework is in place?

If not, how will the Commission ensure that the revised framework adequately protects children’s health and best interests, in accordance with Article 24 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union?

Directive 2014/40/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 3 April 2014 on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products and repealing Directive 2001/37/EC (OJ L 127, 29.4.2014, p. 1, ELI:http://http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/40/oj).
